rows.question: What is a lock in a DBMS?
claims: A lock variable is associated with a data item.
A lock variable describes the status of the data item.
The status described by a lock variable is with respect to the operations that can be applied to the data item.
There is one lock for each data item in the database.
Locks are used to synchronize access to database items.
The access synchronized by locks is performed by concurrent transactions.

rows.question: What is the two-phase locking protocol?
claims: A transaction follows the two-phase locking protocol if all its locking operations (read_lock, write_lock) precede the first unlock operation in the transaction.
That transaction has an expanding (growing) phase.
During the expanding phase, new locks can be acquired.
During the expanding phase, no locks can be released.
The transaction then has a shrinking phase.
During the shrinking phase, existing locks can be released.
During the shrinking phase, no new locks can be acquired.
